title: Customer-vetted model gateways and priority playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable playbook that intake, triages, and prioritizes customer-submitted model requests (new models, variant pins, deprecations, and compatibility eval gates) with explicit lanes for enterprise customers. The output is a small set of operational 'model gateways' (decision checklists and routing rules) that engineering, support, and sales can apply to reduce turnaround time and risk.

Background / Problem:
Enterprise customers are requesting model pins, custom quantized variants, and expedited onboarding. Current handling is ad-hoc: requests land in a backlog, multiple teams ping each other, and decisions (pin vs compatibility vs deprecation) are often delayed or reversed. This causes SLA misses, surprise regressions, and hidden capacity costs. We need an intake and prioritization surface that captures customer non-functional constraints, risk signals, and a deterministic routing path to either: fast-track (sandbox + shadow eval), scheduled onboard (catalog pipeline), or reject/deprecate with a mitigation plan.

Goals:
- Define 3 canonical gateway lanes (Fast‑track enterprise, Standard catalog onboarding, Deprecation/Quarantine) with clear criteria and SLAs.
- Create a prioritization rubric combining customer revenue weight, technical compatibility score, and safety/regulatory risk.
- Standardize eval-gates (unit eval suite + latency/cost delta threshold + regression tolerance) and tie them to automatic routing.
- Document a decision handoff (who approves pins, who signs E2E rollouts, rollback triggers).
- Reduce average enterprise request TTR from ~18 business days to <=7 business days for fast-track lane.
acceptance_criteria: Three documented gateway lanes with scoring thresholds and example requests for each lane
A single intake form and metadata schema that captures: customer tier, revenue signal, data residency, QoS requirements, desired pin duration, and custom privacy constraints
An automated routing prototype (sheet + rules) used in triage meetings that assigns lane and next owner in >=80% of requests without manual override
Eval-gate checklist that includes: compatibility tests, perf regression guardrails (latency + p50/p95), and a quality regression metric; results must be reproducible in CI
Playbook includes rollout, canary, and automated rollback triggers and a documented approver roster (PM, Eng, Security)

decisions: Adopt a 3-lane gateway (Fast-track / Standard / Quarantine) as primary routing model (decision date: 2026-03-07)
Fast-track lane will permit temporary pins up to 30 days with mandatory shadowing and daily quality snapshots
All pinned variants must surface a performance delta matrix (token cost, p50/p95) before approval
Security signoff required only for models flagged by the intake schema (PII/regulatory flag)
tradeoffs: Speed vs Safety: Fast-track reduces time-to-value but increases monitoring burden and potential regressions; mitigated with shadowing and tighter rollback windows
Operational overhead: More structured intake increases initial triage cost but reduces repeated back-and-forth across teams
Capacity vs Cost: Allowing many short-lived pins risks resource fragmentation; we use pin duration limits and CD/usage signals to reclaim capacity
